source_rule: Narrative facts are extracted only from the chapter source files in data/source. External sources are not used to invent narrative facts.

events.description: Takezo is wounded and left among the dead after the Battle of Sekigahara; the chapter recounts the collapse of the Western Army.
Takezo discovers that Matahachi survived and the two reunite on the battlefield.
The two leave the battlefield and spend two days foraging in the Mount Ibuki area.
They travel in what they believe is the direction of Tarui; the text does not establish an arrival in Tarui before the next refuge scene.
Akemi and Oko shelter the two sick stragglers in their mountain house.
Akemi reveals that her family makes and sells moxa and that patrols remain active after Sekigahara.
Takezo goes mushroom hunting in the mountain with Akemi.
Tsujikaze Temma confronts Akemi and demands a share of her family's illicit earnings.
Akemi admits that she scavenges battlefields for valuables and says Temma is believed to have killed her father.
Temma and his men raid the house; Takezo and Matahachi resist them.
Takezo pursues Temma and kills him with the wooden sword.
The final scene establishes that Oko, Akemi and Matahachi have left the refuge together; their destination is not established. Takezo remains behind and discovers the empty house.
The narrative shifts to Miyamoto, where Otsu lives at Shippoji and Takuan is staying at the temple.
Otsu and Takuan walk down to the Aida River to gather flowers for the festival.
Otsu and Takuan go to Ogin's house to collect Otsu's festival obi.
Otsu meets Ogin and learns that the family believes Takezo and Matahachi died at Sekigahara.
Otsu sees Takezo in the crowd during the flower festival; he immediately disappears to avoid capture.
Osugi learns that Takezo has been seen and the Himeji garrison begins an intensified search.
Takezo repeatedly evades the Himeji soldiers and hides in the Sanumo Mountains.
Himeji soldiers raid Ogin's house and arrest her. A villager later reports only a rumor that she is held at Hinagura, so arrival there is not yet confirmed. Otsu witnesses the arrest and escapes.
Takezo secretly tells Osugi that Matahachi is alive and asks her to pass the news to Otsu.
Osugi deceives Takezo into taking a bath while a group of soldiers and villagers surround the house; Takezo escapes.
Otsu receives letters from Oko and Matahachi explaining that Matahachi is alive in another province and intends to marry Oko.
Takuan takes Otsu into the mountains and chooses Itadori Pasture as their camp.
Takezo approaches their camp after hearing Otsu's flute and is persuaded to come to the fire.
Takuan subdues Takezo psychologically and ties him up, completing the promised capture.
Takuan brings the captured Takezo back to Shippoji, and Otsu returns to the temple from the mountain camp.
Takezo is tied to the old cryptomeria tree and the villagers demand punishment; Takuan retains authority over his fate.
Otsu increasingly identifies with Takezo's suffering and begins actively seeking his survival.
Otsu climbs the tree, cuts Takezo free and escapes with him through the mountains.
At Nakayama Pass, Takezo decides to rescue Ogin while Otsu agrees to continue toward Himeji and wait at Hanada Bridge.
Otsu travels alone toward Himeji, becomes ill and collapses at the Mikazuki Teahouse.
Osugi and Gonroku discover Otsu at the teahouse and pursue her; she escapes by diving into a ravine. The later recovery is deferred to chapter 8.
Takezo studies the Hinagura stockade and attacks it to rescue Ogin.
Takezo learns that Ogin was moved to Himeji before his assault.
After escaping the stockade, Takezo heads toward Himeji.
Takezo waits around Himeji, including under and on Hanada Bridge, while trying to locate Ogin.
Takuan finds Takezo and brings him into Himeji Castle.
Takezo appears before Ikeda Terumasa, who accepts Takuan's proposed form of punishment and confinement.
Takezo remains confined in the castle's dark chamber for approximately three years, studying and reflecting.
After three years, Takuan returns and Takezo is released from confinement.
Takezo is renamed Miyamoto Musashi and rejects immediate service as a vassal, choosing to travel independently.
Takuan reports the later whereabouts of Ogin, the continued search by Osugi and Gonroku, and Aoki Tanzaemon's dismissal from Ikeda's service.
Musashi meets Otsu, who has waited for him for three years at Hanada Bridge.
Musashi refuses to take Otsu with him and leaves alone toward the east after leaving her a farewell message.
Seijuro, Toji, Ryohei and the Yoshioka students leave the school for the Kamo River pleasure district.
The Yoshioka group drinks, sings and argues in a pleasure-district house.
Toji and Ryohei separate two students after a fight.
Seijuro leaves the first establishment and Toji follows him to Yomogi while Ryohei remains with the students.
Seijuro and Toji arrive at Yomogi, where Oko and Akemi receive them.
Toji and Oko negotiate privately at Yomogi.
Seijuro drinks and flirts with Akemi at Yomogi.
Oko and Matahachi argue about their marriage while Matahachi remains isolated in a back room.
Akemi interacts with Matahachi within the Yomogi household.
Musashi enters the Yoshioka School after accepting its challenge.
Musashi defeats successive Yoshioka challengers; several disciples are wounded and two later die.
Seijuro and Toji return to the school and assess the aftermath of Musashi's bouts.
Seijuro, Toji, Ryohei and senior disciples deliberate on how to deal with Musashi.
The Yoshioka group attempts a night ambush in Musashi's assigned room.
Musashi escapes through the floorboards and leaves the school by an unestablished route.
Yoshioka pursuers leave the back gate and chase a fleeing figure toward the burned Honnōji ruins.
The pursuers capture Matahachi near Honnōji, mistaking him for Musashi.
Toji recognizes Matahachi from Yomogi and the pursuers discover their error.
Left by the Honnōji moat, Matahachi recognizes Musashi's new name and resolves to warn him.
Denshichiro is reported absent in Ise; this report does not place him physically at the Yoshioka School.
Musashi observes potters in the ceramic district on the road below Kiyomizudera.
Musashi climbs to the Kiyomizudera grounds and stops at a cliff overlooking Kyoto.
A palanquin bearer identifies Musashi and carries the information back toward Chawan Hill.
Porters surround Musashi on the approach to Hongando.
Osugi and Gonroku arrive at Hongando and confront Musashi.
Musashi refuses the family revenge confrontation and walks through the crowd without fighting Osugi or Gonroku.
The crowd searches the Kiyomizudera hills until sunset while Musashi escapes through the wider area.
Jotaro visits the innkeeper at a cheap inn northwest of Kyoto.
Musashi returns to the inn and talks with Jotaro in the hearth room.
Jotaro writes the innkeeper's letter and handles it for Musashi.
Jotaro works at the sake shop, where Matahachi later gives him a letter for Musashi.
Musashi leaves the inn toward Nara and Jotaro follows him.
Musashi passes the Sanjo Avenue security checkpoint.
Musashi and Jotaro reunite on the Daigo mountain road after Jotaro's pursuit.
Musashi and Jotaro stop at Rokuamida, where Musashi writes to Seijuro.
Jotaro turns back toward Kyoto while Musashi continues toward Nara; neither arrival occurs in this event.
Jotaro receives Matahachi's letter for Musashi; no physical meeting between the two men occurs.
Jotaro meets Akemi in the Takase River and Yomogi area and asks about Matahachi.
Jotaro delivers Musashi's message at Yomogi and learns that Matahachi has left.
Jotaro travels south on the Yamato highroad by ox cart toward Mampukuji.
Jotaro loses his bamboo tube near Mampukuji and Otsu helps identify it.
Kizaemon returns Jotaro's lost bamboo tube.
Jotaro, Otsu and Kizaemon travel together toward Uji.
The trio rests at a Uji Bridge teahouse while Kizaemon discusses conditions in Nara with its proprietor.
Otsu chooses the Koyagyu route with Kizaemon while Jotaro continues toward Nara.
Jotaro separates from Otsu and Kizaemon at the Kizu River ferry.
Musashi searches the Abura Hill and Ozoin vicinity for Hozoin.
A young monk directs Musashi through Ozoin toward Hozoin.
Musashi meets Nikkan in the Ozoin garden and is affected by the abbot's spiritual pressure.
Musashi registers at Hozoin as a visiting student.
Musashi watches Agon and the other Hozoin students train in the dojo.
Musashi fights Agon on the dojo floor and kills him.
Nikkan speaks privately with Musashi and explains the lesson about his excessive fighting spirit.
Musashi leaves Hozoin, briefly returns to leave instructions for Jotaro, then proceeds toward Sarusawa Pond.
Musashi takes lodging at a boardinghouse near Sarusawa Pond.
Dampachi, Banryu and Yasubei try to recruit Musashi for public matches, but he refuses.
Jotaro arrives at the Sarusawa boardinghouse with the Yoshioka response and reunites with Musashi.
Inshun is absent during Musashi's initial Hozoin visit; no physical presence is inferred.
Musashi and Jotaro travel from Nara through the Todaiji area toward Hannya Plain.
Musashi positions Jotaro on a nearby knoll to observe the wider Hannya Plain scene.
Musashi recognizes Dampachi's trap and kills him on Hannya Plain.
Hozoin priests and ronin, including Banryu and Yasubei, are encamped around a bonfire.
Musashi fights the ronin group and kills several of its members.
Inshun leads the Hozoin priests in the deliberate purge of the remaining ronin, including Banryu and Yasubei.
Nikkan arrives with five government officials, who inspect the bodies after the battle.
Nikkan explains the purge, advises Musashi and involves Jotaro in rites for the dead.
Jotaro runs from the observation knoll toward Musashi when the Hozoin charge begins.
About ten days after Hannya Plain, Musashi and Jotaro arrive in Yagyu Valley.
Musashi and Jotaro tour the valley and inspect the exterior of Koyagyu Castle.
At Wataya, Jotaro meets Kocha and their teasing becomes a playful physical quarrel.
Musashi bathes with three Kyoto visitors; the narrative identifies Denshichiro among them through Musashi's recognition, but no direct interaction follows.
Musashi, Jotaro and Kocha interact at the inn after the children's quarrel.
Musashi decides to seek a test against the Yagyu name.
Kizaemon's earlier visit to the Kyoto guests is reported in the bath conversation and is not treated as present co-location.
Sekishusai and Otsu discuss flower arrangement and life at the mountain house.
Kizaemon returns from his errand and reports at the mountain-house entrance.
Kizaemon reports delivering the Yagyu response to Denshichiro's party and receives further instructions.
Sekishusai decides to send Otsu to Wataya with a letter and peony instead of receiving Denshichiro.
Otsu rides from the Yagyu estate to Wataya.
Otsu meets Kocha at Wataya and asks for Denshichiro.
Otsu delivers Sekishusai's letter and peony directly to Denshichiro.
Musashi examines the peony stem, reproduces its cut and recognizes the work of an exceptional swordsman.
Otsu rides back toward Koyagyu and encounters Jotaro near the castle and river area.
Jotaro returns to Wataya and gives Musashi Kizaemon's reply letter; Kizaemon is not physically present.
Kocha tends Jotaro's wounds at the inn and stream.
Jotaro and Kocha interact privately in the fodder shed until Kocha's unnamed father interrupts them.
Musashi and Jotaro depart Wataya after Jotaro briefly remains behind to say farewell to Kocha.
Musashi and Jotaro arrive at the main gate of Koyagyu Castle.
Musashi is admitted and taken to Shin'indo while Jotaro is left in the attendants' waiting room.
Kizaemon enters Shin'indo with Kimura, Debuchi and Murata and receives Musashi.
The four Yagyu retainers question and test Musashi during the sake and conversation sequence.
Musashi challenges the hosts to a sword test and they decline to provoke the encounter.
Taro's unusual barking causes Debuchi, then Murata and Kimura, to leave Shin'indo.
Kizaemon learns Jotaro is missing and goes with Musashi toward the disturbance.
Musashi and Kizaemon reach the crowd where Jotaro stands beside the dead dog Taro.
The dog's unnamed keeper attacks Jotaro and Musashi intervenes to protect him.
Musashi challenges the surrounding Yagyu personnel on Jotaro's behalf.
Kizaemon assumes responsibility and orders the crowd to disperse.
Debuchi proposes that Musashi commit suicide and Musashi refuses.
Kimura orders Musashi toward the cells; Musashi instead walks toward the keep and tells Jotaro to wait under a pine in the garden.
Kizaemon and Debuchi try to pull Musashi back while Kimura begins to draw his sword and is restrained.
Musashi declares that he intends to see Sekishusai and challenges the castle to battle.
Kimura accepts the challenge while the senior retainers position themselves around Musashi and Jotaro remains nearby.
Jotaro throws sand to disrupt Kimura's initial sword strike while Musashi evades.
Musashi and Kimura enter a direct sword confrontation while Kizaemon, Debuchi and Murata take positions around them.
Kizaemon, Debuchi and Murata move in together against Musashi.
Otsu's distant flute affects Musashi during the fight; she is not physically present in the castle scene.
Musashi escapes from the castle grounds toward the inner moat and outer darkness; Jotaro is not assumed to remain with him.
Musashi hides by the inner moat after escaping the four retainers.
Musashi searches through the castle woods and valleys for Sekishusai's mountain house.
Musashi reaches the mountain-house gate, reads its plaques and chooses not to enter; no face-to-face meeting with Sekishusai occurs.
Musashi leaves the mountain-house gate and flees toward the wooded Tsukigase-Iga back road.
Otsu and Jotaro search for Musashi on the back road and meet Takuan; Jotaro later turns back for his mask while Otsu and Takuan part.
